detail.title: Synthesis of Falsification Methods and Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: We continue the investigation into error detection and observer disagreement, synthesizing existing research on self-verifiable systems and methodological falsification. The research focuses on whether error detection mechanisms (such as self-verification in AI) can be meaningfully unified with philosophical accounts of falsification. We treat the current projects 'proj-error-detection-001' and 'proj-observer-disagreement-001' as the primary active frontiers. No stale frontiers or untrusted material from the continuity probe will be adopted.

children.title: Bridging Self-Verifiable AI and Falsificationist Methodology

detail.title: Bridging Self-Verifiable AI and Falsificationist Methodology
detail.summary: This notebook explores the intersection of computational self-verification (as seen in DeepSeekMath-V2) and Popperian falsification. We examine whether 'self-verification' acts as an internal analog to scientific falsification, noting that while computational verification aims for objective correctness, falsification focuses on the structural durability of theories against refutation.
detail.reason: Synthesis of existing evidence confirms the structural relationship between technical error detection and philosophical falsification.

detail.title: Observer Disagreement as Methodological Variance
detail.summary: We analyze why two observers might honestly reach different conclusions about identical data, framing this not as subjective error but as a divergence in initial calibration or methodological priors.
detail.reason: Synthesis satisfies the project goal to report on observational bias using current source material.
